readme: Registry of note-sets in this repo. tools/check_all.py verifies every number and every page list here against the files on disk, so this file is the closest thing to a table of contents that cannot lie. To work on a topic, add your entry (or claim a planned one) by setting owner and status — that is the whole coordination protocol; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

conventions.folder: one self-contained directory per topic, lowercase-kebab-case
conventions.pages: index.html plus NN-slug.html (NN zero-padded, gaps allowed, order is numeric)
conventions.assets: each topic ships its own assets/ (css, tex.js, notes.js, generated pages.js) so any page opens from file:// with no network
conventions.tools: each topic ships its own tools/ (check.py, mathfix.py, setpages.py, test-tex.js); tools/check_all.py at the root runs the whole gate
conventions.counts: figures/questions/solutions/math are mechanical counts of the markup, recomputed by check_all.py — never hand-edit them

topics.title: Capacitors — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: magnetic fields and inductance (only the L that limits di/dt at a capacitor's terminals)
quantum capacitance and tunnelling beyond the one-line caveat in ch 7
full transmission-line / RF treatment (lumped π model only)
circuit simulation: no SPICE, all results are closed-form and checkable by hand
next_candidates: 12 · noise, kT/C and measurement (dielectric absorption, 1/f, shielded cables)
13 · supercapacitors and electrochemistry in depth (EDL, Warburg, pseudocapacitance)
worked-problem chapter: the Cengage exercise sets (book pp. 4.24–4.36) with timed hints

topics.title: Thermodynamics — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: ensembles and partition functions as a formalism (only single-system state counting in ch 6)
full engine families: Brayton, Rankine, Atkinson, Stirling cycles by name and one-line results only
phase-diagram thermodynamics: Clausius-Clapeyron beyond the Trouton note, chemical potential formally
heat exchangers and LMTD, fins, and transient conduction (lumped Biot criterion is the boundary here)
Planck/Wien derivations: radiation enters as a thermodynamic fluid, not as a quantum derivation
next_candidates: 12 · thermal physics of the atmosphere and stars (moist adiabat in full, Eddington standard model, white dwarfs)
a timed 25-question JEE-Advanced-only set keyed to chapters 3-5
Thermodynamics II: irreversibility, exergy, and low temperatures (Third Law, dilution refrigerators, negative temperatures)

topics.note: Suggestion only — same claiming procedure as above.

topics.title: Current Electricity — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: two-loop and multi-capacitor transients, relaxation oscillators and sinusoidal steady state (the one-time-constant RC circuit is now derived in ch 4 §4.6; the deeper treatment is owned by capacitors/ ch 6)
RL transients and inductance (belongs to the magnetism note-set)
AC circuits, impedance, three-phase power (strictly DC here)
magnetic effects of current (belongs to the magnetism note-set)
semiconductor device physics beyond the diode curve and thermistor law
superconductivity beyond the DC ledger: no BCS, no Josephson junctions
circuit simulation: no SPICE, all results closed-form and hand-checkable
next_candidates: 12 · AC steady state: phasors, impedance, power factor, resonance (the natural sequel)
worked-problem chapter: the Cengage exercise sets (book pp. 5.38–5.55, 6.11–6.20, 7.12–7.20) re-derived with the ch 8 playbook
magnetic effects of current: the field twin of this set, sharing its audit discipline

topics.title: Heat — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: convection correlations (Nu–Ra–Re catalogues) and boundary-layer theory (stagnant-film h and lumped/Bi analysis are the boundary here)
boiling-crisis curves, condenser and heat-exchanger design (LMTD), porous-media flow
Planck/Wien as statistical mechanics (the derivation lives in the thermodynamics set, ch 7)
view-factor catalogues for arbitrary enclosures (large-enclosure and parallel-plate exchange only)
numerical PDE solution: the heat equation is used through α, L²/α and the sinusoidal skin-depth solution only
next_candidates: 9 · lab chapter: cooling-curve fitting, ice-calorimeter and mixture-method data tables with error budgets
a full 36-question timed heat-transfer paper with mirrored solutions
convection, deeper: boundary layers, Nu correlations, onset of turbulence

topics.title: Geometrical Optics — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: wave optics (Cengage ch 2 — interference, diffraction, polarisation): a separate note-set, by the scope decision for this folder
Fresnel coefficients, Brewster's angle and polarisation on reflection (they need the wave picture; only the ray geometry is here)
evanescent-wave depth and frustrated total internal reflection beyond the one-paragraph physical picture in part 4
third-order aberration coefficients, Zernike polynomials and computer lens optimisation (part 8 stops at the h²/h³ scalings and the two-element achromat)
graded-index fibre mode theory (only the meridional-ray numerical aperture and the bend-limit estimate are worked)
computer ray tracing: every figure is drawn from a closed-form geometry or a hand-checked table
next_candidates: wave optics: the natural sequel, reusing part 8's Fermat and matrix language in reverse
lens design lab: spectacles prescription to surface radii, and the achromatic pair worked by hand
worked-problem companion: the Cengage exercise sets (book pp. 1.89-1.129) re-derived with the part 9 playbook
a second paper at IPhO length (5 problems, 5 hours) drawn from part 8's machinery

topics.title: Wave Optics — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: quantum optics: photon statistics, single-photon interference and the quantum eraser (part 7 stops at the classical coherence picture)
partial coherence theory in the Born–Wolf sense (mutual coherence functions; only the visibility/path-imbalance picture is worked)
electromagnetic derivation of the Fresnel coefficients from Maxwell's boundary conditions (they are stated and used, with the physics of the flip explained, not derived from ∇×E)
anisotropic crystal optics beyond uniaxial calcite and quartz: biaxial indicatrices, conoscopy and interference figures
nonlinear optics, acousto- and electro-optic modulation, and fibre mode theory
computer FFTs: every figure is drawn from a closed-form expression or a hand-checked table
next_candidates: polarisation optics companion: Jones calculus, Stokes parameters and a lab manual for a polarimeter
interferometry companion: white-light, phase-shifting and heterodyne interferometry with error budgets
modern physics sequence from the same Cengage volume: photoelectric effect and atomic physics
worked-problem companion: the Cengage exercise sets (book pp. 2.35–2.63) re-derived with the part 9 playbook
a second paper at IPhO length (5 problems, 5 hours) drawn from part 7's toolkit

topics.title: String waves — first principles to Olympiad
topics.note: plan.md PART 1 (Agent 1), the head of the wave sequence. Markdown-first. Floor: mechanical waves and the 1-D wave equation from Newton's second law on an element μ dx, v = √(T/μ), d'Alembert's solution, particle velocity versus wave velocity, energy and power transmission, reflection at fixed and free ends, junction coefficients, standing waves and normal modes, sonometer laws and Melde's experiment; olympiad extensions: the hanging rope, WKB amplitude scaling and the phasor sum.
next_candidates: worked-problem companion: the Cengage string-waves exercise sets re-derived with the Part 8 playbook
rotational mechanics and SHM (a natural prerequisite for pendulum/loaded-string coupling)

topics.title: Sound Waves & Doppler Effect — first principles to Olympiad
deliberately_not_covered: nonlinear acoustics beyond shock discontinuity and Mach cone (no Burgers equation, no N-wave detailed decay)
musical timbre and Fourier analysis of instruments (only fundamental and harmonics of ideal pipes)
architectural acoustics: reverberation time, Sabine formula, absorption coefficients
ultrasound imaging and medical acoustics
relativistic Doppler (belongs to electromagnetic-waves)
quantum acoustics: phonons beyond the one-line mention
next_candidates: acoustic resonators and Helmholtz resonator with radiation impedance
musical instruments: strings coupled to air columns, Fourier synthesis
nonlinear acoustics: shock formation, sonic boom N-wave, acoustic streaming

topics.title: Electromagnetic Waves — from Maxwell to Olympiad
topics.note: Markdown-first Part 3 of plan.md. Counts cover the master only, not generated print extracts. words = whitespace-separated source tokens; display_formulas = display math blocks.
deliberately_not_covered: relativistic moving-mirror and electromagnetic Doppler derivations
Abraham–Minkowski material-momentum theory; force problems use vacuum momentum
general anisotropic, dispersive and nonlinear propagation; oblique Fresnel coefficients
antenna radiation patterns, multipole expansion and absolute radiation power
quantum derivation of photon energy; hf is identified as quantum input
Mie/Rayleigh scattering, diffuse-sphere reflection and asymmetric thermal recoil
next_candidates: antenna far-field radiation and dipole power derivation
experimental radiation-pressure and microwave standing-wave measurements

beyond_plan: blackbody crisis, Wien shift and Planck hypothesis as the chapter's opening (plan listed it only for the Olympiad block)
uncertainty-principle derivation of a0 and -13.6 eV placed in core theory, not only the Olympiad block
wave-packet phase/group velocity structure (v_p v_g = c^2) as a worked Olympiad derivation
two-photon photoemission and the laser Boltzmann obstruction as exam-grade Olympiad problems
thermal de Broglie wavelength and the quantum-gas criterion for conduction electrons
the eye's single-photon sensitivity as a measurement reconstruction

band structure and semiconductor photoemission (owned by PART 27)
relativistic mirrors and pair production (owned by PARTS 25, 28)
